review_notes:
I read the whole file and the related declarations in Mathlib/MeasureTheory/VectorMeasure/BoundedVariation.lean (the simp lemmas vectorMeasure_Icc, Ioc, Ioo, Ico and so on) and Mathlib/Analysis/BoundedVariation.lean (BoundedVariationOn.bilinear_comp, smul, mul).

The only simp attributes in the file are on rightLim_bilinear_comp and leftLim_bilinear_comp. Together with the existing vectorMeasure_Icc/Ioc/Ico/Ioo simp lemmas, they rewrite (hf.bilinear_comp hg B).vectorMeasure s into B (f.rightLim b) (g.rightLim b) - ... The direction is canonical, since the leftLim or rightLim of a composite becomes a composite of leftLims or rightLims. They cannot loop, because the right-hand sides contain no leftLim or rightLim of a B-composite. The hypotheses hf and hg are genuinely needed, because the one-sided limits of a non-BV function are junk values. They are discharged by the `simp [hab, hf, hg]` calls that use them. The ext_of_Icc call in vectorMeasure_bilinear_comp_eq' passes `simp [hab]` with hf and hg only as local-context hypotheses.

I found no competing rules or unwanted expansion. I also found no missing canonical simp lemma that the file's own uses would need.

Two points I considered and did not report. The lemmas are stated as function equalities rather than pointwise, but the file's own simp calls compile with them, so a pointwise version would be speculative. They also do not fire for `f * g` or `f • g`, which are not syntactically of the form `fun x ↦ B (f x) (g x)`. The file does not rely on that.

I did not run Lean, so remaining uncertainty is only about how the discharger behaves in untested uses.
